concepts.title: Nature of Learning: Change Brought by Experience

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Nature of Learning: Change Brought by Experience' refers to.
questions.a: Learning is any relatively permanent change in behaviour or behaviour potential that results from experience or practice -- not from maturation, fatigue or drugs. It shows in doing, but also in knowing: changed capacity counts as learning even before it is performed.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nature of Learning: Change Brought by Experience'.
questions.a: Learning is experience-written change -- relatively permanent, practice-made, and more than performance.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Classical and Operant Conditioning' refers to.
questions.a: Conditioning explains learning by association and consequence. In classical conditioning a neutral stimulus paired repeatedly with a significant one comes to evoke its response -- Pavlov's dogs salivating to a bell. In operant conditioning behaviour is strengthened by reinforcement and weakened by punishment -- consequences shape future action.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Classical and Operant Conditioning'.
questions.a: Learn by pairing, learn by payoff -- associations teach anticipation, consequences teach repetition.

concepts.title: Observational Learning and Cognitive Forms of Learning

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Observational Learning and Cognitive Forms of Learning' refers to.
questions.a: Not all learning needs direct reinforcement. Observational learning copies models -- children imitate what they watch, for better or worse; insight learning solves problems by sudden reorganisation of the field; and verbal learning shows how words and associations are memorised. Cognition thus joins conditioning in the full picture.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Observational Learning and Cognitive Forms of Learning'.
questions.a: Watch, understand, reorganise -- learning also happens without reward, by example and by insight.
